# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Thursday, November 19, 2026

Morning edition for Thursday, 19 November 2026 (IST). Covers Wednesday 18 Nov to early Thursday. Stock and index figures are Wednesday 18 Nov closes. IBJA rows are the 18 Nov PM session; AGLOC's 19 Nov block was posted that morning.

IBJA's 19 Nov AM session was not posted at writing time (the page reads "Rates will be uploaded soon"), so every IBJA row below is the 18 Nov PM session.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Gold slide hits gold-loan stocks: Muthoot Finance −3.97%, Manappuram Finance −4.59%
Gold fell for a third straight session on 18 November. MCX December gold futures stood at ₹1,31,207 per 10 g, down ₹3,016 (−2.25%), which PTI described as the lowest level in over a year. Comex December gold futures fell $91.30 (−2.36%) to $3,772.90 an ounce. PTI and Business Standard attribute the move to a stronger US dollar, at a 19-month high, and expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, ahead of the FOMC minutes.

Gold-loan stocks fell with it on the NSE close. Muthoot Finance, a listed peer and a separate company from Muthoot Fincorp, fell 3.97% to ₹2,640.00. Manappuram Finance fell 4.59% to ₹283.00. CNBC-TV18 reported that Manappuram had fallen 12.9% over five sessions and Muthoot Finance 10.5% over four.

Business Standard said the fall "raised concerns over collateral values, asset quality and the impact of tighter loan-to-value regulations". It reports that Muthoot Finance's Stage 3 assets rose more than twofold to ₹7,267 crore and its Stage 2 assets rose to ₹23,467 crore, citing the post-results analyst call. Those are Muthoot Finance figures. They are not Muthoot Fincorp's.

Manappuram Finance's management said the following to CNBC-TV18. Chairman and managing director VP Nandakumar said the company's loan-to-value is below 65%, so auctions are expected to be limited to 2% of the book. He said only about 1% of Stage 2 assets are expected to move to Stage 3, and Stage 3 is expected to fall to 1% as customers adapt to revised repayment norms. Stage 2 may stay at 5% to 8% before declining gradually. These are the company's expectations, not reported results. Manappuram's Stage 2 gold-loan assets rose to about 5% of its gold-loan portfolio in the September quarter, from about 0.5% in the quarter before.

On the rule side, Business Standard quotes SBI Securities' Sunny Agarwal describing a revised LTV calculation for bullet-repayment loans: the total amount due at maturity counts, and renewal is allowed only after accrued interest is paid. That is an analyst's description, not a new instrument; the rules check is in the Rules file.

Sector scale, per CNBC-TV18 citing CRIF High Mark: India's gold-loan market is ₹23.3 lakh crore, growing more than 60% over the past year. Q2 FY27 fresh gold-loan originations were ₹8.15 lakh crore by value, up 27.2% year on year, while the number of accounts originated fell 4.1% to 369.4 lakh. NBFCs' share of originations was 31.4%, up about 4 percentage points quarter on quarter.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a lower gold price lowers the per-gram value of pledged collateral, so loans written close to an LTV ceiling have a thinner cushion. Muthoot Fincorp is a gold-loan NBFC. Its newest asset-quality figure in the sources checked is Stage III at 1.07%, from its Q2 filing of 14 Nov, which came before this fall. The Stage 2 and Stage 3 build described above is at Muthoot Finance, a listed peer.

### IIFL Finance: Fairfax sells 13.24% in a ₹3,488.1 crore block at ₹617
FIH Mauritius Investments, the Fairfax India entity, sold 5.65 crore equity shares of IIFL Finance in an 18 Nov block deal. That is 13.24% of IIFL Finance's paid-up equity, for ₹3,488.1 crore at ₹617 a share. Forty domestic and global institutional investors bought. SBI Mutual Fund was the largest buyer, with 81.53 lakh shares (1.91%) for ₹503.04 crore.

The pre-deal term sheet had indicated up to 56.53 million shares at a floor of ₹611, about ₹3,454 crore. The executed price was ₹617, so the executed figures are the ones to use.

IIFL Finance closed at ₹661.95 on the NSE, up 4.01% from ₹636.40.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked. The sale is a shareholder transaction in another NBFC's shares.

Sources: Moneycontrol, 18 Nov 19:43 IST, https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/block-deals-fairfax-india-sells-rs-3-488-crore-worth-of-iifl-finance-shares-rimco-india-nippon-india-sbi-mf-among-40-buyers-14083718.html · Mint, 18 Nov 09:43 IST (pre-deal term sheet), https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/iifl-finance-share-price-nbfc-stock-jumps-6-after-rs-3-454-cr-block-deal-why-is-fairfax-selling-entire-13-25-stake-11794973879183.html

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

Indian shares fell on Wednesday 18 November. The Nifty 50 closed at 25,227.95 (−0.63%), Nifty Bank at 62,038.65 (−0.38%) and Nifty Financial Services at 27,992.25 (−0.72%). Business Standard puts the Sensex at 82,031.81, down 500.38 points (−0.61%). Nifty Midcap 100 fell 1.22%, Nifty Metal 2.46%, Nifty Consumer Durables 3.13% and Nifty IT 1.24%. Nifty PSU Bank rose 0.59%. India VIX closed at 15.57, up 0.29%.

Provisional NSE flows: foreign investors bought ₹17,913.16 crore and sold ₹12,046.38 crore, a net buy of ₹5,866.78 crore. Domestic institutions bought ₹14,602.25 crore and sold ₹17,762.15 crore, a net outflow of ₹3,159.90 crore.

Listed gold-loan and NBFC peers, NSE close on 18 Nov: Muthoot Finance (a listed peer) ₹2,640.00, −3.97%. Manappuram Finance ₹283.00, −4.59%. IIFL Finance ₹661.95, +4.01%. Shriram Finance ₹970.00, −1.31%. Bajaj Finance ₹1,093.85, −2.43%. Muthoot Microfin (a group company) ₹165.17, −2.22%.

The rupee closed at 93.4450 per US dollar, with a reported change of +0.03% (Business Standard; Reuters carried 93.44). Brent settled at $91.95 a barrel on the ICE January contract, down $1.19 (−1.28%), per Reuters and Dow Jones settlement data carried by Euronext.

### Muthoot Microfin board meets today: a dated item, no result yet

Muthoot Microfin's board meets today, Thursday 19 November 2026, on audited half-year accounts. Those accounts feed Muthoot Fincorp's restated consolidated statements. This is a dated event. No outcome is known at writing time, and nothing in this edition reports one.

Muthoot Fincorp's investor page, fetched at 07:08 IST today, carries no document dated after 14 Nov 2026. The announcements list is partly loaded by script, so this is "no new filing seen", not confirmation that nothing was filed.

Standing facts (original dates; not new today):

- Q2 FY27 (Reg 52), filed 14 Nov 2026: PAT ₹779.41 crore for July–September. H1 PAT ₹1,485 crore on total income of ₹6,567 crore (PTI, via BusinessLine). Stage III 1.07% (vs 1.41% a year earlier, per ET). CRAR 19.38%.
- The same 14 Nov board meeting recommended CCCPS conversion (40,00,00,000 CCCPS) to shareholders, and the reappointment of Thomas John Muthoot, Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot for five years from 1 Feb 2027. No meeting date for the CCCPS resolution has been announced.
- IPO: up to ₹3,000 crore fresh issue, at the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) stage, filed Aug 2026. The sources checked give no filing link for this item, so none is cited here.

Dated items that are not Muthoot Fincorp filings: SEBI's Credit Risk-o-Meter goes live on 21 Nov, and the RBI monetary policy committee meets on 2–4 Dec 2026.

### SEBI chairman on margin trading: a press statement, not a decision or a circular
On 18 Nov, SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said SEBI continues to consider proposals to strengthen the margin trading facility, but has not taken a decision. He also said he does not see feasibility in extending market hours. Business Standard reported these remarks.

This is a statement to the press. It is not a decision and not a circular, and nothing in it is an imposed rule. The same day, the chairman gave an address at the 65th WFE General Assembly. That is a speech, not an instrument.

Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Thursday, 19 November 2026 (IST)

Morning edition for Thursday, 19 November 2026 (IST). Covers Wednesday 18 Nov to early Thursday. Stock and index figures are Wednesday 18 Nov closes. IBJA rows are the 18 Nov PM session; AGLOC's 19 Nov block was posted that morning.

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new RBI, SEBI or IBBI instrument on 18 Nov changes a rule that applies to Muthoot Fincorp. What was checked is set out below. A representation to RBI is not a rule change, and the items under "Other 18 Nov items" are not instruments.

What was checked between 18 Nov and early 19 Nov: the RBI notifications feed, where the latest instrument is still the 11 Nov Reserve Bank of India (Domestic Money Transfer) Directions, 2026 (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S843/02-27-019/2026-27), with nothing new on 18 or 19 Nov; the RBI press releases of 18 Nov, all routine liquidity and retail items (the result of the overnight VRRR auction held that day, an overnight VRRR under LAF on 19 Nov, the SGB 2020-21 Series II premature redemption price due 19 Nov at ₹13,345 per unit, the Treasury Bill auction results, and Money Market Operations as on 17 Nov), none of which is a rule; SEBI's circular list, whose latest entry is dated 17 Nov on the margin framework for the commodity derivatives segment, not NBFC lending ([SEBI circular](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/review-of-margin-framework-for-commodity-derivatives-segment_105799.html)), with no circular dated 18 Nov; SEBI's press-release list, where the latest is PR No.73/2026 of 16 Nov and nothing is dated 18 Nov; SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey's address at the 65th WFE General Assembly on 18 Nov, which is a speech, not an instrument ([SEBI speech](https://www.sebi.gov.in/media-and-notifications/speeches/nov-2026/address-by-shri-tuhin-kanta-pandey-chairman-sebi-65th-wfe-general-assembly-and-annual-meeting-building-markets-for-the-future-growth-trust-and-resilience-_105806.html)); and IBBI, where no new instrument for NBFCs appeared and the latest dated item on the page is 10 Nov 2026.
Sources: [RBI notifications feed](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx) · [RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [SEBI circular list](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebiweb/home/HomeAction.do?doListing=yes&sid=1&ssid=7&smid=0) · [IBBI](https://ibbi.gov.in/)

### Other 18 Nov items (reported, not rule changes)

- SEBI chairman on margin trading. Business Standard reports that SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on 18 Nov that SEBI continues to consider proposals to strengthen the margin trading facility, but has not taken a decision. He also said he does not see feasibility in extending market hours. This is a statement to the press. It is not a decision and not a circular, and it imposes nothing.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none stated in the sources checked.
Sources: Business Standard, 18 Nov 16:44 IST, https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/sebi-considering-proposals-to-strengthen-margin-trading-facility-chairman-126111800596_1.html

- Gold-loan LTV calculation for bullet-repayment loans. Business Standard, quoting SBI Securities' Sunny Agarwal, describes a revised LTV calculation for bullet-repayment loans. The total amount due at maturity is taken into account, and renewal is permitted only after accrued interest is paid. The 18 Nov instrument check above found no new RBI instrument, and the sources checked do not name the instrument this calculation comes from. It is an analyst's description, not a rule stated here.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: unclear. Muthoot Fincorp is a gold-loan NBFC, but the sources checked do not say whether this calculation applies to its loans.
Sources: Business Standard, 18 Nov 19:46 IST, https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/gold-price-slide-drags-muthoot-finance-manappuram-shares-down-nearly-4-126111801259_1.html


### Limits of this check

- A representation to RBI is not a rule change. Gold-loan lenders' requests that RBI review a rule are asked, not granted. No RBI response to any such request is reported in the sources checked, and no RBI instrument on 18 Nov changes one.
- No SEBI or RBI instrument dated 19 Nov is in the sources checked. The check covers the 18 Nov feeds and the 19 Nov morning only.
- Dated items, not instruments: the Muthoot Microfin board meets on 19 Nov 2026 on audited half-year accounts; its outcome is not reported here. SEBI's Credit Risk-o-Meter goes live on 21 Nov 2026. The RBI monetary policy committee meets on 2–4 Dec 2026.
- Muthoot Fincorp's own filings are not in this section. Its latest filing in the sources checked is the Q2 FY27 filing of 14 Nov 2026, which is covered in the News file with its original date.
